name: Tudor & Jacobean

description.short: The transitional century in which English building acquired Renaissance ornament without surrendering its medieval plan and silhouette.
description.long:
Between the end of the Wars of the Roses and the arrival of Inigo Jones, English architecture took on classical motifs — pilasters, strapwork, shaped gables — while keeping medieval massing, medieval framing, and the medieval hall. The result is a hybrid that later purists disliked and that later revivalists loved precisely because of its irregularity.

The transmission channel is worth noting: the ornament arrived largely through Netherlandish engravings and immigrant craftsmen, not from Italy directly. It is a second-hand Renaissance, which explains its cheerful indifference to proportional correctness.

defining_characteristics: Renaissance ornament applied to medieval massing and plan
Tall multi-flued chimney stacks and large mullioned, transomed windows
Strapwork and shaped gables transmitted via the Low Countries
The H- and E-plan great house with hall at the centre
